expect.why: the `## Passages` section is last, below the APPEND marker, and its one block is well formed: an ISO 8601 timestamp no earlier than the entry, an author who may write, and a witness stated by value
the witness digests to the Observation section as commit 01 held it, and the held prose is a contiguous run of that section
the note the prose came out of names no entry, and the digest document that cites this one is not the document the ground pins, which is how every by-value seed here is built
the lift moved the section the ground is anchored to, and the reading verdict at commit 02 states the digest of the section as the lift left it

note: the shape every other passage seed is a deformation of: prose lifted out of an artifact at commit 02, the witness naming the section as commit 01 held it, and a reading verdict discharging the drift the lift itself caused. A `## Passages` section is optional, so every other seed in this corpus is a near-negative for the optionality rule and this one is the positive: a tail section that is present is held to its place in the order. The citing sentence sits in a second document rather than in the section the ground pins, because an artifact anchored by value may carry no entry id — a consistent rename of every id in a seed is a transformation the corpus holds itself invariant under, and it would move the digest of any section with an id inside it. That a real lift leaves the citation where it was is held by `tests/test_passages.py::test_a_line_carrying_a_citation_is_never_taken`, and the rule about where a citation belongs by D60 and K28.
history: apply commits/01, commits/02, … as successive commits in a fresh repository; expectations name the commit they apply to. `@commitNN` in an entry is substituted with the real short object id of that commit before it is made, because a seed cannot know an id the runner has not created yet
